name: 80 x 56 mm server fan, 12 V
summary: A high static pressure 80 mm fan for 2U servers and storage, with PWM control and tach output. Sample data: the supplier and every figure here are fictional.

buyers: Data center operators replacing failed fans
demand.reason: India's data center capacity is set to triple from 1.6 GW in mid-2026 to 6 GW by 2029, and the India data center cooling market is forecast to grow several times over by 2035. Fans are the moving part in air-cooled servers that wears out.

sources.title: JLL India data centre 2026 mid-year report
India data center cooling market outlook, Grand View Research

checked: Speed, airflow, pressure, current and bearing type as stated by the supplier
notChecked: Any measurement, no sample received yet

parts.name: Fan frame
parts.role: Hold the motor and shape the airflow.
parts.whatItDoes: A square moulded frame with a round venturi, four mounting corners and struts that carry the motor hub.
parts.whyItMatters: Venturi shape and blade clearance decide how much pressure the fan can build against dense heatsinks.
buyingChecks: Ask for the plastic and its flammability rating
Check the mounting holes and frame depth against your chassis
Ask for the tip clearance

parts.name: Driver board
parts.role: Run the motor and report its speed.
parts.whatItDoes: A small ring board in the hub with the motor driver chip and the Hall sensor. It reads the PWM speed signal and sends back a tach pulse.
parts.whyItMatters: The driver sets how the fan behaves when a signal is lost and whether it restarts after a stall. Both matter for server uptime.
buyingChecks: Ask what speed the fan runs at with no PWM signal
Ask for locked-rotor protection and restart behaviour
Ask for the driver chip maker and origin

parts.name: Stator
parts.role: Make the field that spins the impeller.
parts.whatItDoes: A small wound steel stator on a bearing tube in the hub. The impeller's magnet ring turns around it.
parts.whyItMatters: Winding and steel quality set power draw. At thousands of fans per hall, a watt each adds up.
buyingChecks: Ask for current at rated speed
Ask for the winding insulation class
Ask for efficiency at the operating point

parts.name: Ball bearings
parts.whatItDoes: Two small ball bearings in the stator tube that the impeller shaft runs in.
parts.whyItMatters: Bearing life usually sets fan life. Sleeve bearings cost less and fail sooner in hot servers.
buyingChecks: Ask for the bearing type: dual ball or sleeve
Ask for rated life at 40 C and at 70 C
Ask for the bearing maker

parts.name: Magnet ring
parts.role: Turn with the impeller around the stator.
parts.whatItDoes: A bonded magnet ring inside the impeller hub.
parts.whyItMatters: A weak or cracked ring lowers torque, so the fan cannot hold speed against back pressure.
parts.material: Bonded ferrite or neodymium in a steel cup
buyingChecks: Ask for the magnet material
Ask for the magnet origin
Check the ring is retained, not only glued

parts.name: Impeller
parts.whatItDoes: A moulded hub with seven swept blades and a steel shaft. It spins at up to 16,000 rpm.
parts.whyItMatters: Blade shape trades airflow, pressure and noise. Balance sets vibration, which harms nearby hard drives.
buyingChecks: Ask for the PQ curve at your operating speed
Ask for balance grade
Ask for the blade material and its temperature rating

parts.name: Cable and connector
parts.role: Bring power and PWM in, send the tach signal out.
parts.whatItDoes: A four-wire lead for 12 V, ground, PWM and tach, ending in a keyed connector.
parts.whyItMatters: Pinouts vary between server makers. A wrong pinout is the most common reason a replacement fan does not work.
buyingChecks: Check the pinout against your board
Ask for cable length options
Ask whether a hot-swap carrier is available
